result.title: Communication-Efficient Distributionally Robust Federated Averaging with Multi-Source Data
result.summary: Federated learning trains a shared model from distributed client data. The deployment risk is typically specified through two approximations: each unknown local distribution is replaced by its empirical distribution, and the unknown deployment mixture across clients is replaced by empirical or prescribed training weights. Existing robust methods usually address one approximation at a time through local distributional ambiguity sets or worst-case client mixtures. However, joint treatment of both approximations remains underexplored. To address this gap, we construct a global ambiguity set formed by admissible mixtures of client-wise Wasserstein ambiguity sets, yielding a distributionally robust optimization formulation. The construction allows client-dependent ambiguity radii, preserves client-wise separability of the objective function, and yields a high-probability out-of-sample guarantee for the resulting robust problem. We then introduce a penalty-based approximation of this formulation and develop a communication-efficient algorithm called BiDRO-FedAvg, for which we establish a convergence guarantee. We validate the proposed framework through a market-demand prediction simulation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文针对联邦学习中局部经验分布与客户端混合权重两重近似带来的部署风险，构造由各客户端 Wasserstein 模糊集混合而成的全局模糊集，给出 DRO 形式与高概率泛化保证，并提出带惩罚近似的通信高效算法 BiDRO-FedAvg 及其收敛分析。
